newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Skanska says 1997 profit can match 1996.
newsitem.headline: Skanska says 1997 profit can match 1996.

text.p: Swedish construction company Skanska managing director Melker Schorling said on Wednesday that profits this year should match 1996 levels.
"It is not impossible to keep 1996 profit levels in 1997, excluding the sale of shares in Graningeverken," Schorling told a seminar.
Skanska on Tuesday posted a 1996 profit after financial items of 5.17 billion crowns compared to 2.57 billion in 1995.
Schorling forecast a weak construction market in Sweden.

"Official forecasts for the building market in Sweden feel a little high. The Swedish market is extremely tough just now. We will struggle on with cost savings...and hopefully make a little money," Schorling said.
The outlook for the group's real estate division was more positive.
"The real estate operations result will increase in 1997...lower building, lower interest rates and higher activity increases rents and prices," Schorling said.
International operations were positive for Skanska, Schorling said.

"We have been extremely fortunate in the U.S.. We have good experience with acquisitions in the U.S. and can imagine making more...The important thing is to be strong on local markets. And we are in New York and Atlanta just now," he said.
"We see no limit to how big we can become in the U.S....the limit is how fast our organisation can grow. But I don't believe we will experience the enormous growth that we have so far," he said.
For its industrial construction division, Schorling said the company plans acquisitions in eastern Europe.
"We are planning several acquisitions in Eastern Europe. Several discussions are ongoing and are far along," he said.
